title: Appendicitis in a child
subtitle: Score, ultrasound, then decide

sources.title: Diagnosis and treatment of acute appendicitis: 2020 update of the WSES Jerusalem guidelines (World J Emerg Surg 2020;15:27)
Holcomb and Ashcraft's Pediatric Surgery: appendicitis

sources.org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
sources.title: Intravenous fluid therapy in children and young people in hospital (NG29)

red_flags.text: A child under five with abdominal pain and fever. Perforation rates are high in young children because the history is poor and the omentum is short.
Generalised peritonitis, a rigid abdomen or septic shock.
Diarrhoea with pain and fever: pelvic appendicitis is frequently misdiagnosed as gastroenteritis.
Pain that settles then returns with fever and a mass: an appendix abscess.

do_now.text: Analgesia at a weight-based dose. Analgesia does not mask the signs and makes the examination more reliable.
Septic or peritonitic child: intravenous access, fluid resuscitation at the NICE NG29 bolus volume, and broad-spectrum antibiotics per local protocol.
Paediatric surgical review for any child with a high clinical score or peritonism.

assess.text: Calculate a validated score. The Paediatric Appendicitis Score and the Appendicitis Inflammatory Response score help rule out and stratify, but they do not make the diagnosis alone.
Migration of pain, anorexia, pain on hopping or coughing, right iliac fossa tenderness, fever.
Consider the alternatives: mesenteric adenitis, gastroenteritis, urinary infection, constipation, testicular or ovarian torsion, lower lobe pneumonia, Meckel diverticulitis.

investigate.text: Full blood count and C-reactive protein; urinalysis; pregnancy test in post-menarchal girls.
Ultrasound is the first-line imaging in children. Report should state whether the appendix was seen.
CT is reserved for the child with an equivocal ultrasound and a persisting high suspicion; MRI where available is a radiation-free alternative.
Low-risk score and a well child: discharge with safety-netting or a planned review rather than imaging everyone.

resuscitate.text: Isotonic maintenance fluids while nil by mouth, with glucose and electrolytes checked.
Pre-operative antibiotics per local protocol, continued post-operatively only for complicated appendicitis.

definitive.text: Appendicectomy, laparoscopic where expertise allows, for uncomplicated and complicated appendicitis.

Non-operative management with antibiotics is an option in selected children with uncomplicated appendicitis on imaging, discussed with the family including the risk of recurrence. An appendicolith predicts failure.
Appendix abscess in a stable child: antibiotics with or without image-guided drainage; interval appendicectomy is not mandatory.

escalate.text: Paediatric anaesthesia and surgery for young children. A district hospital without paediatric anaesthesia should transfer the under-fives after resuscitation.
Paediatric intensive care for septic shock.
Gynaecology input when the adnexa are a realistic alternative in an adolescent girl.

notes: In a young child, the time from symptoms to perforation is short. A child sent home must leave with a clear plan for review, not a vague reassurance.
Scores are best at ruling out and identifying the child who needs imaging. They do not replace a surgeon's examination.
Ultrasound is operator-dependent. A report that the appendix was not seen is not a report that the appendix is normal.
